text:
marie.ops: Hi team — onboarding a new parent in our Amsterdam office and they asked about how parental leave paperwork differs for EU hires vs US. Also taxes on company top-up? any quick pointers?
people-ops: Great q. High level: core Redwood benefits (leave length, top-up eligibility) apply across locations but legal paperwork and payroll tax handling differs by country. For NL specifically we need the UWV/doctor note and the local parental leave form filled by the manager + employee.
people-ops: For tax: in many EU countries the payroll top-up is treated as regular salary and subject to payroll taxes/social contributions locally. In the US some jurisdictions also tax top-ups; payroll team handles withholdings per local law.
people-ops: Link to country checklist: https://redwood.intra/hr/international-parental-checklist (use the NL tab for Amsterdam)
alex.eu: @people-ops to confirm: do we require employee to sign anything for data transfer to payroll in the EU? GDPR consent?
people-ops: Yes, include the 'international HR data transfer' acknowledgement on the leave form for EU citizens; we partner with local payroll providers who are DPA-compliant. People-ops will attach DPA summary when we send approval email.
payroll-uk: Payroll note (UK): statutory pay rules differ. If we're applying a company top-up, we run it through payroll as a separate pay element called 'Parental Top-Up' and code it for tax. Pensionable? Depends on the contract; confirm with benefits team.
payroll-us: US payroll: we withhold federal/state taxes on top-ups. If the employee is on unpaid FMLA and we top up, the top-up is regular wages. For multi-country employment, we need the local payroll vendor to process local withholdings.
marie.ops: Thanks  and what about benefits continuation (health/dental) during unpaid portions?
people-ops: We maintain benefits enrollment for up to 12 months for Redwood-sponsored plans. In some countries employee contributions still apply; for US folks we offer COBRA options and we assist with premium billing. For EU, if the country requires employer contributions while on statutory leave, payroll will calculate employer side and we'll notify the hiring manager.
dan.mgr: Operational ask: while they're out, who covers interview panels scheduled this month? I can step in but need to know expected phased-return hours if any.
marie.ops: Good point — they've tentatively requested a 3-day/week phased return for 8 weeks starting after 8 weeks post-birth. I'll add that in the leave form.
people-ops-bot: reminder: Submit international-parental-leave packet and attach passport/placement certificate within 30 days of leave start to ensure local filings.
people-ops: I'll coordinate a 10-min sync with payroll-uk/payroll-us and local HR rep to confirm tax treatment and payroll codes. @marie.ops we'll copy you and the employee.
marie.ops: Thanks everyone. If we could get the payroll code names (so offer letters and manager handover are consistent) that would be super helpful.
people-ops: Will send a follow-up email with the precise pay element names and the country checklist within 24 hours.
